items.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001
items.q: you went from John Coltrane to singing that Leonard Cohen was it?

ctx.x: It just made my skin really tough because there was something stronger than their words, and that was that I really was, in my heart I really felt that what I was doing was correct and that’s what I followed.

Yeah. Well if we were to look at your list of songs from this evening, you went from John Coltrane to singing that Leonard Cohen was it? But they all sound like they seemed to mesh together really well.

It’s all music to me. I’ve always believed that music should be without boundaries. And for me jazz, having a foundation in jazz music really kind of allowed me to be a part of different kinds of music, much like the musicians that were performing, or that created this fusion music. And I just felt that if you could take the popular tunes of the 40s and turn them into jazz standards then there was a possibility that with these new other forms of these other songs, or even songs that I write could even have a kind…
